newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Houston-Angola flights planned by U.S. firms - source.
newsitem.headline: Houston-Angola flights planned by U.S. firms - source.

text.p: A U.S.-based airline, possibly Tower Air of Texas, is planning to fly from the Houston area to Angola's capital Luanda via the Cape Verde Islands to service the oil industry, business sources said on Wednesday.
"The plan, as I understand it, is to fly passengers and cargo from Houston to Cape Verde, change planes and then on into Luanda," one U.S. businessman in Luanda told Reuters.
"I don't know the specifics of the deal but Tower Air is involved and TAAG will also be involved," the businessman said.
Analysts in Luanda said the stopover in Cape Verde would allow for the transfer of cargo for oil businesses based in Port Harcourt, Nigeria, and other parts of the West African coast.
TAAG, the Angolan national carrier, confirmed the plan was under consideration but declined to give specifics.
"We have been reviewing this plan for some time now, but it is very early in the planning stages now -- far too early to talk about it," a TAAG official said.
Currently, oil industry employees have to travel on flights via Paris or Gatwick to West Africa and then onto Angola if they are flying in from Houston.
U.S. company oil executives have told Reuters that the new route could cut their costs for cargo transport, but would not save them much on the cost of flying their staff.

"We move in and out of here several times a week. I know it sounds like a good idea but the problem is, when people leave here they don't just go to Houston or even the States, they go all over the world. It wouldn't necessarily save us any money," said one oil executive.
